title: Michigan City's pier light and the Sheridan keepers: the lake took their parents in 1878

sources.what: 'On March 15, 1878 Aaron and Julia along with their youngest son Robert were returning from the mainland in a small boat owned by island fisherman Chris Ankersen. Just off the ice-locked lighthouse shoreline, the boat overturned, and Aaron, Julia and Robert drowned in the frigid water.' Ankersen clung to the boat and was rescued. 'The remaining Sheridan children were raised by their grandparents Henry and Julia Moore in Kendall County Illinois. George Sheridan became a professional lighthouse keeper and served in Chicago, Michigan City, Indiana and Saugatuck, Michigan.' Julia: assistant keeper 1872-1878; Aaron: keeper 1866-1878.
sources.who: National Park Service, Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore, 'Aaron Sheridan' (photos credited Jack Sheridan, 2007; last updated April 10, 2015)

sources.what: 'tragedy struck the Sheridan family in March of 1878, Julia, Aaron and their youngest son Robert were returning to the island when their boat capsized. All three drowned.' Julia was 'the very first Assistant Keeper'. 'In 2006, the family placed grave stones for Julia, Aaron, and Robert in the island cemetery.'
sources.who: National Park Service, 'South Manitou Island Cemetery'

sources.what: Passengers: Aaron, Julia, their infant son Robert and island fisherman Christ Ancharson. Chicago Tribune, March 19, 1878 (reprinted South Haven Sentinel, March 23): 'When within one mile of the island the boat capsized'; 'The Norwegian clung to the boat, and his cries for help brought a man out in a skiff, who rescued him.' Bodies 'never recovered'. Levi (about 12) and George (about 10) 'apparently watched helplessly from atop the lighthouse tower.' Five orphaned boys went to their maternal grandparents in Illinois.
sources.who: Dianna Stampfler, 'Tragedy on South Manitou Island', PromoteMichigan, March 15, 2021 (from her book Michigan's Haunted Lighthouses, ch. 3)

sources.what: Aaron A. Sheridan, keeper 1866-1878: 'March 15, 1878 he was drowned in a boating mishap on a return trip from the mainland. Also drowned was his wife Julia Moore Sheridan and his youngest son Robert. Their bodies were never recovered.'
sources.who: Find a Grave, Aaron A Sheridan (memorial maintained by Jack Sheridan)

sources.what: Richard Kitchen's letter: the keeper Mr. A. A. Sheridan and Mrs. Julia Sheridan 'were drowned in the lighthouse boat at 6 o'clock last evening, while coming from Glen Arbor and within a mile from the lighthouse.' George Sheridan, their son, 3rd assistant at Chicago Harbor from March 3, 1896; 'on April 1, 1905, George became the 1st assistant keeper at the newly built Michigan City East Pierhead Lighthouse'; head keeper of Kalamazoo River Lighthouse from June 1, 1909. Phillip Sheridan (son of Lyman Sheridan, Aaron's cousin): head keeper of Point Betsie from November 1895, then head keeper of the Michigan City East Pierhead Lighthouse from January 1, 1919 until his retirement on August 1, 1930.
sources.who: Lighthouse Digest, 'Memorial Marker Recalls Tragedy, Honors Legacy'

sources.what: George H. Sheridan (born 1868, died 1915): Chicago Harbor 3rd assistant 1896-1899; Calumet Pierhead 1st assistant 1899-1905; Michigan City East Pierhead 1st assistant 1905-1909; Kalamazoo River principal keeper 1909-1914 (Register of Lighthouse Keepers).
sources.who: U.S. Lighthouse Society Archives, Kraig Anderson Inventory of Lighthouse Personnel

sources.what: Michigan City East Pierhead: the light moved to the east pier on October 20, 1904, in an octagonal metal tower atop a fog-signal building; keepers used the elevated walk. First assistants: George H. Sheridan (1905-1909). Head keepers: Thomas J. Armstrong (1904-1918), Philip Sheridan (1918-1930), Walter A. Donovan (1930-1940).
sources.who: Kraig Anderson, Lighthousefriends, 'Michigan City East Pierhead Lighthouse' and 'Old Michigan City Lighthouse'

sources.what: 'Baker was replaced by George Sheridan, who was transferred-in after four years as First Assistant Keeper at the Michigan City Pierhead Light.'
sources.who: Terry Pepper, Seeing the Light, 'Kalamazoo River Lighthouse' (sources include Jack Sheridan)

sources.what: Assistant keepers at Michigan City included George Sheridan.
sources.who: Old Lighthouse Museum (Michigan City Historical Society), 'About'

sources.what: South Manitou: Aaron, Julia and 'ten-month-old baby Robert' were returning in their sailboat, which capsized about a mile from the island; the oldest boys 'ran up and down the beach weeping'; the five surviving sons went to grandparents in Illinois.
sources.who: Kraig Anderson, Lighthousefriends, 'South Manitou Island Lighthouse'

sources.what: Kalamazoo River: keeper George H. Sheridan, whose parents drowned in 1878.
Michigan City East Pierhead Light and elevated walk, constructed 1904; the building was 'painted buff' until about 1920.
sources.who: National Register of Historic Places nomination, Michigan City East Pierhead Light Tower and Elevated Walk

sources.what: Head keeper Phillip Sheridan, Michigan City East Pierhead, until 1930.
sources.who: U.S. Coast Guard History, 'Michigan City East Pierhead Lighthouse'

sourcing_note: The year Phillip Sheridan took over Michigan City differs (Lighthousefriends 1918, Lighthouse Digest Jan. 1, 1919), so the narration says only 'until 1930'. That the two oldest boys watched from the tower rests on one account (Stampfler, 'apparently'); Lighthouse Digest's other article says the two children searched the shore; the narration says 'one account says'. The weather differs (Stampfler: a late-afternoon squall; the fisherman's own account: pleasant weather, then a sea capsized the boat), so no storm is drawn; the time (Kitchen's letter, 6 p.m.; Stampfler, late afternoon) allows a dusk sky. No people are drawn in the boat or the water. The 'Grey Lady' caption Scoop forwarded on Nov. 15 had no source for any Grey Lady at this light, so this short is the sourced pier story instead. Independent check Nov. 15: the tower-watching line was cut (Lighthousefriends says the boys ran up and down the beach, Lighthouse Digest that they searched the shore, Stampfler only 'apparently' the tower), replaced by the five sons going to grandparents in Illinois; 'kept' became 'helped keep' (George was first assistant); Phillip/Philip is spelled both ways, so the narration says only 'another Sheridan'; the island light is drawn dark in beats 3-4 and 5 (no source says it was lit); the 1905 picture of the pier building is darkened (the National Register says it was painted buff until about 1920).

beats.text: In 1878, Lake Michigan took a lighthouse keeper, his wife and their baby. One of their sons later helped keep Michigan City's pier light.
beats.label: MICHIGAN CITY, INDIANA
beats.credit: NPS, Sleeping Bear Dunes; Lighthouse Digest; Lighthousefriends

beats.text: Aaron Sheridan kept the South Manitou Island light. His wife, Julia, was his assistant keeper.
beats.label: SOUTH MANITOU ISLAND, MICHIGAN
beats.credit: National Park Service; Dianna Stampfler, PromoteMichigan

beats.text: On March 15, 1878, they were coming home from the mainland in a small boat with their son Robert and a fisherman.
Within a mile of the island, it overturned in icy water. The fisherman was rescued. The Sheridans drowned.
beats.credit: Chicago Tribune, March 19, 1878, via PromoteMichigan; NPS

beats.text: The lake never gave them back. Their five other sons were sent to grandparents in Illinois.
beats.credit: National Park Service; Dianna Stampfler; Lighthousefriends

beats.text: One of them, George, grew up to keep lights too. In 1905, he became first assistant keeper of Michigan City's new pier light.
beats.label: GEORGE SHERIDAN
beats.credit: Lighthouse Digest; U.S. Lighthouse Society; Seeing the Light

beats.text: Another Sheridan ran that light until 1930.
beats.credit: Lighthousefriends; U.S. Coast Guard History; Lighthouse Digest
